description: Fig. 8 is a six-panel composite of bright-field TEM micrographs with selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) insets from Fe-17.5Mn-1.5Al-0.58C TWIP steel at two tensile-strain states: (a-c) after straining at 0.02, (d-f) after straining at 0.05. (a) Two-beam image with g = (111), 100 nm scale bar, dark defect clusters lying along a yellow dashed grain boundary labelled "G.B."; an SAED pattern is inset top-right. (b) The same boundary region with g = (3̄11), its own SAED inset and 100 nm scale bar, four red arrows marking line defects near the boundary. (c) A 50 nm-scale close-up in which yellow arrows point at dense dark clusters (stacking faults). (d) A 500 nm-scale overview of two grains labelled "Grain A" and "Grain B" separated by "G.B.", with two yellow circles numbered 1 and 2 and white arrows indicating the (111) and (1̄11) directions. (e) A 20 nm-scale image labelled "Twins": a yellow arrow runs along the twin growth direction and red arrows mark twin starting points. (f) An indexed SAED pattern, "Zone axis // [011]", overlaying a blue hexagon labelled "Grain A" with a red hexagon labelled "Twin". Together the panels argue that dislocation activity at the austenite grain boundary first produces stacking faults (0.02) and then deformation twins that grow into the grains (0.05).

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a two-beam bright-field TEM micrograph (100 nm scale bar) in which dark, elongated defect clusters lie along a yellow dashed line annotated 'G.B.', with an inset SAED pattern and the diffraction condition 'g = (111)'.

Panel (b) is imaged with 'g = (3̄11)' (100 nm scale bar) and carries four red arrows pointing at straight, line-like defects close to the yellow dashed grain boundary labelled 'G.B.', plus its own SAED inset.
Panel (c) is the highest-magnification micrograph (50 nm scale bar) and shows dense dark clusters marked by yellow arrows.

Panel (d) is a 500 nm scale-bar overview containing two grains labelled 'Grain A' and 'Grain B' separated by a line marked 'G.B.', with two yellow circles numbered 1 and 2 and arrows indicating the (111) and (1̄11) directions.
Panel (e), 20 nm scale bar, is annotated 'Twins'; a yellow arrow indicates the twin growth direction and red arrows mark the twin starting points, as stated in the caption.

Panel (f) is an indexed SAED pattern with 'Zone axis // [011]' in which a blue hexagon labelled 'Grain A' and a red hexagon labelled 'Twin' are overlaid to show the twin/matrix orientation relationship; labelled reflections include (1̄1̄1), (2̄00), (1̄11) and (200).
The caption states that panels (a-c) correspond to straining at 0.02, where stacking faults and Frank partial dislocations on the (111) plane are indicated by red and orange arrows.
The caption states that panels (d-f) correspond to straining at 0.05, where deformation twins formed near the austenite grain boundary and gradually grew into the grains.

Caption/pixel disagreement: the caption assigns red and orange arrows to panels (a-c), but the supplied pixels show red arrows only in (a) and (b) while (c) uses yellow arrows; (a) carries a white rectangular box rather than an arrow annotation.
The caption gives the alloy as Fe-17.5Mn-1.5Al-0.58C while the citing sentence gives Fe-17.5Mn-1.5Al-0.85C for the same Hong et al. [86] study; the carbon content disagrees between the two sources.
The citing text states that Hong et al. [86] concluded the prior austenite grain boundary provided the nucleation sites for deformation twins.

The citing text states that at a tensile strain of 0.02 various slip systems were activated near the austenite grain boundary and that interaction of mobile dislocations produced Shockley and Frank partial dislocations slightly away from the prior austenite grain boundary, forming stacking faults.

The citing text states that strong dislocation movement and deformation twins together contributed to the high strain hardening of TWIP steels; it phrases 0.02 and 0.05 as strain-rate values whereas the caption phrases them as strains.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar, showing dark elongated defect clusters aligned along a yellow dashed line labelled 'G.B.' (grain boundary). A top-right inset is an SAED pattern; a white rectangle frames the analysed area. Text beside the inset reads 'g = (111)'.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the boundary region with a 100 nm scale bar and SAED inset labelled 'g = (3̄11)'. Four red arrows point at dark line-like defects adjacent to the yellow dashed boundary marked 'G.B.'.
Higher-magnification TEM image, 50 nm scale bar, of dense dark clusters; five to six yellow arrows point at these clusters, which the caption assigns to stacking faults.

Lower-magnification TEM micrograph, 500 nm scale bar, spanning 'Grain A' and 'Grain B' separated by a boundary marked 'G.B.' Two yellow circles labelled '1' and '2' mark regions inside the grains; white arrows define the (111) and (1̄11) directions.

TEM micrograph, 20 nm scale bar, labelled 'Twins': a thick band is annotated with a yellow arrow running along its length and three red arrows marking its lower edge/start points; parallel fringe-like bands run across the field.

Indexed SAED pattern with 'Zone axis // [011]'. Two overlapping hexagons are drawn: a blue one labelled 'Grain A' and a red one labelled 'Twin'; reflections are labelled with indices including (1̄1̄1), (2̄00), (1̄11) and (200).

unreadable_items: panel (f): a few reflection indices around the hexagon edges are only partially legible at the supplied resolution
panels (a) and (b): the SAED inset spot patterns themselves are not annotated beyond the g-vector line, so individual reflections cannot be indexed
arrow colour coding in panels (a)-(c) could not be reconciled with the caption's 'red and orange arrows' wording
